newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba lukewarm on EU plan to press for change.
newsitem.headline: Cuba lukewarm on EU plan to press for change.

text.p: Cuba said on Thursday it was not ready to comment on a European Union plan to step up pressure for change on the island but its foreign policy would not be guided by interference in its internal affairs.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Miguel Alfonso, asked about the EU plan at a weekly news briefing, told reporters Cuba had not been officially informed of the document approved last Monday by EU finance ministers.

But he made several comments about Cuba's general views, indicating Havana was hostile to attempts from abroad to seek reform of its one-party Communist system and in particular to countries that seek to put conditions on better relations.

"Pre-conditioning works in detriment to relations," he said. "Cuba's foreign policy is determined by the principles of non-interference in internal affairs and absolute defence of its sovereign equality with the rest of the world."

The EU move came just days after Cuba angrily accused EU member Spain on Nov. 26 of meddling in its internal affairs and withdrew official approval for a new Spanish ambassador. Spain's conservative government has criticised President Fidel Castro's government in recent weeks and had proposed a tougher common EU stance on Havana than the version that was approved.

The EU plan calls, among other things, for members to step up reminders to Cuban authorities of "fundamental responsibilities on human rights, in particular freedom of speech and association." It contains a note of conditionality, saying "the EU considers that full cooperation with Cuba will depend upon improvements in human rights and political freedom".

EU leaders have been under pressure from the United States to stiffen their stance towards Havana, which Washington hit with tougher economic sanctions after two U.S. civilian aircraft were shot down by Cuba in February. The EU remains firmly opposed to the sanctions.
